Alex.feeling: Fairly comfortable: Finley is clearly the cat and the table is converging on him.

Blair.feeling: Messy: Finley's admitted Mouser claim and Ellis's contradicted Tit visit look strongest, but Alex's Owl report and the day's pile-on make me want a second check before the vote.

Casey.feeling: Confusing: my Hawk hit on Finley gave no egg, which clashes with his Mouser claim, and I'm dead and can't speak.

Drew.feeling: Round 3 feels tense but fairly readable: Finley admitted Mouser, Ellis's Tit claim contradicts Alex, and Casey's death leaves the table split on the second cat.

Ellis.feeling: Tense: the table is turning on me, and my teammate Finley is exposed.

Finley.feeling: Tense and messy: I've openly claimed Mouser, the table is now throwing at me, and the Floofer is still unidentified between Ellis, Blair and Alex.

Casey.note: Table consensus is Finley. Banking the cards is worth more than keeping them, except the Wild.

Drew.note: Finley is the admitted Mouser and Meowfia, so I'll throw at Finley. I'll throw D6 and W1 for two votes and keep my high cards.

Ellis.note: Throw at Blair, a Farm player: the best card is recovered if we lose and banked if we win.

Finley.note: Three players are throwing at me, so I need the most votes on a Farm player. I'll throw several cards at Blair, who has an unverifiable Turkey claim, to pull the vote away from me.

Alex.confusing: How a Wink death interacts with the throw: the dead player still throws cards that bank, but their votes don't count. Also it was unclear what a Pigeon visit does to the egg counts that everyone cross-checks.
Alex.fun: Round 3, when my Owl report listing Floofer, Kookaburra and Mouser visitors let the table pin down both cats quickly, and then watching the vote land on Finley.
Alex.change: Make the Meowfia more able to coordinate or learn each other, or give them a better way to bluff. As the lone cat in round 1 I had almost nothing to build a convincing cover story on.
Alex.regret: In round 1 I claimed Pigeon and said I hit Finley, which contradicted his +2. I should have claimed a role whose result I could fit to the known egg counts, such as Tit or Falcon with a quiet visit, and not accused the player whose count was already explained.

Blair.confusing: The Storyteller's dawn reports and claim-checking were clear, but it was hard to verify Tit, Eagle, and Floofer claims because nobody could see a visit log.
Blair.fun: Round 2 was the most fun: Ellis's visitor list and Drew's dodging made the Mouser hunt feel real, and the 8-vote throw at Drew was satisfying.
Blair.change: Let players see a public visit log, or privately confirm their own visit results, so Tit and Floofer claims can be checked instead of argued.
Blair.regret: In round 3 I threw my cards at Finley, but I should have pressed harder on Ellis, the Floofer whose Tit visit claim contradicted Alex's Owl report.

Casey.confusing: Nothing major. The only unclear part was how the Owl's visitor list and the Wink death fit together in round 3, since the Wink's source wasn't visible.
Casey.fun: Round 2, when my Eagle report listed Ellis's visitors. Working out who the Mouser was from the visitor lists felt like real deduction.
Casey.change: I'd show who died, or at least whether a Wink was used, so the Wink gives more to work with. I'd also soften the runaway lead, since banking big cards early made the rest of the game feel decided.
Casey.regret: In round 3 I visited Finley as the Hawk without any real reason, and I learned nothing. I would have picked someone the table was less sure about, like Ellis or Blair, to get information that would have helped sort the Floofer.

Drew.confusing: Whether a dead player's throw still counts toward a team's score and how the losing-side consolation returns your highest card were unclear until I saw the results. The day's flow of who was dead and who could still vote was also hard to track.
Drew.fun: Round 1 was the most fun: Alex's shifting Pigeon story unravelled as the table checked Finley's +2 against each visit, and the 10-vote eggsecution felt like a real verdict.
Drew.change: I would make the dawn reports name the nest changes of every player each night, so cross-checking claims is easier. The Meowfia count being hidden also made late-round throws feel like guesses.
Drew.regret: In round 2 I used my Wink on Ellis, who was a Farm Falcon, to silence an accuser, which gave away my Mouser role for nothing. I would hold the Wink and keep my claim vague until the vote was clearly against me.

Ellis.confusing: How a Meowfia player's throw scores when the team loses: only the best card comes back if you threw at the other team, which made round 3's throw choice hard to evaluate.
Ellis.fun: Round 2, when I worked out from the Owl's list of visitors that Drew had to be the Mouser. The table then converged on him, even though I got winked right after.
Ellis.change: Let Meowfia learn something about each other, or give the Floofer a way to check the claims it hears. Playing blind as a cat was mostly guesswork.
Ellis.regret: In round 3 I claimed a Tit visit to Alex, which Alex's honest "nobody visited me" quickly disproved. I should have claimed a role whose visit couldn't be checked against someone else's nest. For example, I could have claimed the Pigeon and named a target who had stayed quiet.

Finley.confusing: How the Wink and dead players' throws interact. Casey was winked, yet still threw 5 cards at me, and it was unclear whether those count toward the total.
Finley.fun: Round 1's Eagle-versus-Pigeon cross-check, where Alex's claim collapsed against my exact +2 egg count and the table voted him out 10 to 1.
Finley.change: Make the day's wink reveal clearer, so the table knows whether a dead player's throws still count and who is dead.
Finley.regret: In round 3 I openly claimed Mouser, then threw 4 cards at Blair, so I lost cards and the table learned my role. I would stay quiet or claim a Farm role and keep my cards.
